name: Mebeverine + Chlordiazepoxide
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; Chlordiazepoxide: Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.
Yellow crystalline powder (base); hydrochloride is soluble in water.

Mebeverine Hydrochloride: A second-generation papaverine analogue synthesised around the same time as verapamil; not approved in the USA. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1965 (Duphar, Netherlands). Chlordiazepoxide: The first benzodiazepine, discovered by chance by Leo Sternbach at Roche in 1955. First approval/introduction: Patented 1958; approved 1960 (Hoffmann-La Roche).
IBS symptoms are often triggered or worsened by anxiety. Mebeverine relieves spasm; chlordiazepoxide reduces anxiety-driven gut hypersensitivity.

Mebeverine Hydrochloride Direct action on GI smooth muscle (blocks sodium channels and calcium influx), relieving spasm without affecting normal gut motility; no systemic anticholinergic effects. Receptor / target profile: Direct musculotropic action on GI smooth muscle; blocks sodium channels and reduces calcium influx; local anaesthetic effect; minimal anticholinergic activity.

Chlordiazepoxide Enhances GABA-A mediated inhibition in the limbic system, reducing anxiety and associated autonomic/visceral symptoms. Receptor / target profile: Acts on benzodiazepine allosteric sites of GABA-A receptors, producing anxiolytic, sedative, anticonvulsant and muscle-relaxant effects.
Completely absorbed but extensively hydrolysed (parent undetectable in plasma)
Esterase hydrolysis to veratric acid and mebeverine alcohol, then demethylation
~1.1 h (mebeverine alcohol); demethylated carboxylic acid ~2.5 h (PR)
Summary: Rapidly and completely absorbed; extensive first-pass hydrolysis to veratric acid and mebeverine alcohol. Prolonged-release form allows twice-daily dosing.
Hepatic – to desmethylchlordiazepoxide, demoxepam, desmethyldiazepam, oxazepam
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 0.5–4 h. ~96% protein bound. Metabolised to active desmethylchlordiazepoxide, demoxepam and desmethyldiazepam. Half-life 5–30 h (active metabolites much longer).
Functional abdominal pain with psychological component
One tablet three times daily before meals
Short-term use (2–4 weeks) due to benzodiazepine component
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Not recommended under 10–18 years (varies by formulation).
Use the lowest dose (5 mg two to four times daily max); avoid where possible (Beers list).
Exclude organic disease if new symptoms in patients >40 years
Dependence – limit to short courses; taper
Accumulation in elderly and hepatic impairment
Mebeverine Hydrochloride: CNS excitability possible; supportive care. Chlordiazepoxide: Somnolence, confusion, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
See doctor if new symptoms after age 40, weight loss or rectal bleeding
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
